newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gintian B shares surge on takeover plan.
newsitem.headline: Gintian B shares surge on takeover plan.

text.p: Shenzhen Gintian Industry Co Ltd's B shares surged in the afternoon session after the conglomerate announced a plan to buy a domestic power plant for 80.94 million yuan, brokers said.
The B share was trading at HK$4.10 at 0620 GMT, up HK$0.30 or 7.89 percent.
"Investors bought Gintian anticipating that the acquisition would boost Gintian's operations in the long term," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said.
"But investors seem to be too enthusiastic about the plan," the analyst said, citing a net loss of 62.10 million yuan based on international accounting standards posted by Gintian for 1996.
Gintian's A shares hit their 10 percent limit up of 11.70 yuan soon after the afternoon session opened.

Gintian, which is currently involved in real estate development, textiles and foreign trade, announced on Tuesday it would buy the Linzhou Coal-fired Power Plant in central China's Henan province to further diversify its business.
Gintian said it would pay the amount in three equal annual installments starting in November 1998.
The plant had net profits of 12.30 million yuan on sales of 140 million yuan in 1996, it said.

The plant's pre-tax profits are likely to reach 40 million yuan this year against 18 million yuan in 1996. It was given approval by local authorities last October to raise electricity rates to 340 yuan per megawatt from 270 yuan, Gintian said.
Trading in Gintian's A and B shares was suspended on Tuesday morning pending the announcement.
